_comment: Conventions + cheat-sheets for the text-to-world semantic-map pipeline. NOT a fixed class list — the per-scene class catalog is fully dynamic. This file provides: (1) the intent_type taxonomy (the only TRULY fixed part), (2) a hex-picking algorithm so per-scene classes get distinct colors, (3) genre cheat-sheets as inspiration, (4) optional 'common conventions' for universal terrain (grass/water/dirt) that authors can adopt or override. Revised 2026-05-25 to remove the medieval-bias of v1.

terrain_shader.description: Ground cover that becomes a biome on the ground shader (ADR 0055). One big plane, NOT per-pixel objects.
examples_across_genres: grass, dirt, sand, snow, ice, mud, lava, void, water_surface (universal)

terrain_displacement.description: Vertex displacement via heightmap.png (ADR 0052). NOT encoded as a color in the semantic map — listed instead in heightmap_hints.high_regions / low_regions.
examples_across_genres: hill, valley, ridge, crater, river_bed, pond_bottom, cliff, plateau, terrace

object_placement.description: Discrete entities spawned at extracted positions. The semantic map color marks WHERE; the catalog name + description tells the asset gen WHAT.
examples_across_genres: house, wall, tower, bridge, statue, market_stall, well, fountain (medieval/town)
altar, brazier, chest, pillar, throne, trap (dungeon)

hex_picking_algorithm.principle: Pick hexes that are visually + spectrally distinct so a downstream CV / LLM extractor can color-threshold them apart.
rules: Each class gets ONE hex. No reuse.
Pairwise hue spacing: any two class hexes should be ≥25° apart in HSV hue, OR ≥0.25 apart in saturation/value if hues are close.
Prefer SATURATED colors (saturation ≥ 0.5) for object_placement so they stand out against terrain.
Prefer DESATURATED colors (saturation 0.3-0.6) for terrain_shader so they read as 'background' against the saturated objects.
Avoid pure black (0,0,0) and pure white (255,255,255) — they're often used as 'no data' or 'overflow' markers.
Avoid colors within 30 luminance units of each other if their hues are close — they'll quantize to the same bin under JPEG noise.

starting_hue_anchors._purpose: Sensible defaults so common terrain types get conventional colors. NOT required — override when the scene aesthetic demands it (tundra grass might be #b0c8a0, lava lake might be #f04020).

genre_cheat_sheets._purpose: Per-genre common-class suggestions. Used by yume-scene-class-catalog to bias class selection when the scene brief + reference indicate a particular genre. NOT enforcement — Claude should ADD scene-specific classes beyond these.

medieval_town.palette_warmth: warm (terracotta, ochre, deep green, slate grey)

sci_fi_colony.palette_warmth: cool (silver, white, ice blue, regolith grey, accent emergency orange)

modern_city.palette_warmth: neutral (asphalt grey, glass blue, concrete white, accent yellow/red signage)

dungeon_interior.palette_warmth: dark (charcoal, deep red, torch amber, mossy green)

alien_world.typical_topography: varied — depends on the world's geology
alien_world.palette_warmth: saturated unusual (teal, violet, magenta, electric green, bioluminescent cyan)

post_apocalyptic.palette_warmth: desaturated (rust orange, ash grey, dirt brown, accent radioactive green)

natural_wilderness.palette_warmth: natural (greens, browns, sky blue, accent berry red)

underwater.palette_warmth: blue-green (deep blue base, accent yellow coral, red fish markers)

class_count_guidance.why_a_max: Past ~32 hexes, color separation in the semantic map becomes unreliable under JPEG noise + gpt-image-2's slight color jitter. If a scene genuinely needs more classes, group adjacent concepts ('small_house' + 'medium_house' → 'house' with size range) before adding more colors.
class_count_guidance.object_size_class_split: Some games want to distinguish house sizes or building types. Solution: emit 2-3 hexes in the SAME hue family (e.g. small_house #c04020, large_house #a02020, civic_building #c02040) — close enough to extract as 'building' family, distinct enough to subclass.

_authoring_note: Stage 2 (yume-scene-class-catalog) reads this file as conventions, not enforcement. The skill picks classes per-scene driven by the brief + reference + genre cheat-sheet (when applicable) + the hex-picking algorithm. Common terrain gets conventional hexes (grass=#a0d870 etc) by default; specific aesthetic intent in the brief overrides them. Class count is dynamic 6-32, not capped at 14.
